title: Verifier verdict
description: The document a verifier writes on stdout, on exit code 0 only. A non-zero exit means the verifier itself failed and reached no verdict; stdout is then undefined and must not be parsed. See SPEC.md sections 1.1, 2 and 4.

verdict.description: The decision. Two values, no third. There is deliberately no 'error' value: a verifier that reached no verdict exits non-zero instead (SPEC.md section 1.1).

profile.description: Echoes the request's profile. A mismatch is a conformance failure. The reason_code namespace must equal this value — a cross-field constraint not expressible in draft 2020-12, checked by the conformance runner.

reason_code.description: A registered code from SPEC.md section 7, namespaced by profile. Required when verdict is 'fail'. Singular by design: when several signals fire at once, this names the primary one under a precedence the profile documents, and evidence carries all of them (SPEC.md section 4.1).

detail.description: Human-readable. Never parsed by a consumer. May be empty on a pass.

evidence.description: Profile-defined objects. May be empty; a pass may carry evidence and often should. Evidence identifies and characterises — ids, counts, rates, signal names — and never reproduces the candidate (SPEC.md section 6). Order is part of the determinism guarantee (SPEC.md section 8).

then.description: A fail must carry a reason code. Enforced here rather than in prose, because a fail without a code is a verdict a consumer cannot route on, and routing on verdicts is what the contract is for.
